Run `npm test` before pushing.

history.task: Stop dropping jobs that exhaust every attempt
history.summary: A job that runs out of attempts is now parked in a dead letter list instead of vanishing, so a failed job can still be inspected after the fact.

history.task: Split the growing-delay maths out of the policy module so the scheduler can reuse it
history.summary: Lifted the exponential delay maths into src/scheduler/backoff-policy.ts and left src/retry-policy.ts as a thin re-export, so the worker and the scheduler share one implementation. The exported ceiling is BACKOFF_CEILING_MS.
decisions: Delay maths belongs to the scheduler package; the policy module only decides whether another attempt happens at all

tests.summary: delay cases pass against the new module path

history.task: Write down how the API hands a job to the queue
history.summary: Documented the enqueue path in the readme so a new contributor stops guessing at the shape of a job.

edits.README.md:
# Fanout queue

A small background job queue for the fanout service. The API enqueues a job,
a worker picks it up, and a failed job is put back with a growing delay.

## Enqueueing

Call `enqueue` with an id, a payload, and an attempt count of zero. The worker
owns everything after that.

Run `npm test` before pushing.

history.task: Find out why the worker burns CPU when nothing is queued
history.summary: Measured the empty-queue loop and found the worker busy-waits rather than sleeping. Left the fix open because it needs a real timer in the scheduler.

history.task: Raise worker concurrency for the nightly fanout run
history.summary: Raised nightly worker concurrency from two to six once the queue was ruled out as the bottleneck; throughput on the fanout run roughly tripled.

query: I cannot find the helper that works out how long a failed job waits before its next attempt. Where did it move to, and what was the old constant called?

designedLoss.rationale: The old identifiers only ever existed on the removed side of the move commit. RepoMind's deterministic extractor turns decisions, passing commands, and the summary into memories and never the diff, so the deleted names are unreachable for it. full-history carries the diff verbatim and answers the question outright.
